subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate non-blocking heartbeat execution lane, and what session-state and delivery-ordering guarantees must it preserve?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it would change heartbeat execution ownership, run ordering, session state, and message delivery semantics, so automation should not choose the durable product contract alone.

options.title: Define heartbeat isolation contract
options.body: Approve a design for a distinct heartbeat execution model that preserves session-state ownership, delivery ordering, retry behavior, and tool side-effect boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Keep current serialized model
options.body: Continue using skip-and-retry plus isolated/light context controls and rely on narrower fixes such as retry cadence to reduce user-visible stalls.

options.title: Defer until narrower fixes land
options.body: Let the open retry-cadence and activity-idle work land first, then reassess whether a full non-blocking lane is still needed.

recommendation.title: Define heartbeat isolation contract
recommendation.body: Approve a design for a distinct heartbeat execution model that preserves session-state ownership, delivery ordering, retry behavior, and tool side-effect boundaries before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history trail for the unified heartbeat runner and retry-cadence behavior that this product decision would replace or extend.
